message.content:
I’m afraid Google Cloud does **not** offer an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU for Compute‑Engine instances.  
Google’s GPU catalog currently includes:

| GPU family | Models | Typical memory |
|------------|--------|----------------|
| NVIDIA Tesla T4 | `nvidia-tesla-t4` | 16 GB |
| NVIDIA Tesla P100 | `nvidia-tesla-p100` | 16 GB |
| NVIDIA Tesla V100 | `nvidia-tesla-v100` | 16 GB |
| NVIDIA A100 | `nvidia-a100-80gb` | 80 GB |
| NVIDIA A100 | `nvidia-a100-40gb` | 40 GB |

If you need a high‑performance GPU similar to the RTX A6000, the **NVIDIA A100** (especially the 80 GB variant) is the closest match available on Google Cloud.

---

## Example: Create a Compute‑Engine VM with an NVIDIA A100 GPU (80 GB)

Below is a **gcloud CLI** command that creates a VM running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with one NVIDIA A100‑80GB GPU.  
Feel free to adjust the machine type, zone, and other flags to suit your workload.

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-gpu-instance \
    --zone us-central1-a \
    --machine-type n1-highmem-8 \
    --subnet default \
    --network-tier PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model STANDARD \
    --service-account default-compute@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    --scopes https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 200GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
    --boot-disk-device-name my-gpu-instance \
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        apt-get update
        apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470
        reboot' \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-a100-80gb,count=1 \
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the instance will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration (`n1-highmem-8` = 8 vCPU, 52 GB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Base OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS). |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Size & speed of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach a GPU (`type=nvidia-a100-80gb,count=1`). |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Bash script that runs on first boot (installs NVIDIA driver). |
| `--service-account` | IAM service account for the instance. |
| `--scopes` | OAuth scopes for the instance. |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Allows the instance to use any reservation (optional). |

> **Important:**  
> * You must enable the **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** in your project.  
> * Billing must be enabled.  
> * The GPU quota for your region must allow at least one A100‑80GB GPU.  
> * After the instance boots, you’ll need to SSH into it and run `nvidia-smi` to verify the GPU is visible.

---

## REST API Alternative

If you prefer to use the REST API directly, here’s a minimal JSON payload you could POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances`. Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your values.

```json
{
  "name": "my-gpu-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a100-80gb"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default-compute@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send this payload with an authenticated POST request to the Compute Engine endpoint.  
After creation, you can query the instance status via GET requests.

---

### Bottom line

* **RTX A6000** is not available on Google Cloud.  
* Use **NVIDIA A100‑80GB** instead if you need comparable performance.  
* The gcloud CLI example above is the quickest way to spin up such an instance.
